enhanced_information: Cones are mainly located in the fovea centralis, providing high visual acuity and responsible for color vision due to containing photopigments like iodopsin. They have three types (red, green, blue) for color discrimination and synapse with bipolar cells to transmit visual information to the brain. The cones are not necessarily located only in the peripheral retina, and their sensitivity is not necessarily less than the rods. They have membranous discs stacked in their outer segment and synapse with bipolar cells, not ganglionic neurons or only center bipolar 'on'.
analysis: Cones are primarily located in the fovea centralis, not necessarily in the peripheral retina. They contain membranous discs stacked in their outer segment and are responsible for color vision. Cones have high sensitivity and are not necessarily less sensitive than rods. They synapse with bipolar cells, not ganglionic neurons or only center bipolar 'on'.
